_comment: Scheduling policy only — never benchmark configuration. What runs is
decided entirely by the benchmark's progress.json; this file only says
what resources to ask Slurm for.
split    prefer one task per part where the run allows it. It only
takes effect when that run's own options say part_based:true;
a whole-object run is always a single task.
gres     Slurm --gres value. Note the 2080 Ti pool is 11GB, which is
under both the ~13GB ns2s resident worker and VNS's measured
12.4GB, so those need the H200 slices or the A6000s.
An adapter with no entry here uses 'default', so a benchmark naming an
adapter this file has never heard of still schedules.

ns2s.why: seconds per part; splitting would cost more in scheduling than it saves

sf3d.why: runs its proxy adapter on the GPU in-process, so it needs a card despite uses_gpu=False

vns.why: 12.4GB measured; full Ampere cards beat 1/7 H200 slices for a long compute-bound loop
